title: The Prefigurement of Resurrection in Lazarus
english: A discourse by Amphilochius, Bishop of Iconium, concerning the four-day Lazarus. Bring again the evangelist John into the midst, for it is good to observe the firstfruits of the resurrection. For you heard him recently saying: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom he raised from the dead (John 11:1-44). Did you see the firstfruits of the resurrection prefigured in Lazarus, which the faithful crowd recognized?

The crowds recognized, and the chief priests turned the miracle into malice. Thus they acted with malice toward the resurrection of Lazarus, because after his resurrection, which you heard, they consulted to kill him. Did you see excessive malice? The one whom the Lord raised, they themselves resolved to kill, not realizing that even if they kill, the Lord would again lightly raise the friend. They consulted to kill Lazarus; nothing so unsettled the Jews as the resurrection of Lazarus. Only this miracle they were not able to slander.

They slandered the sight of the blind man born from birth, saying: 'This is he; this is not he; he is like him.' They slandered the raising of the daughter of Jairus, saying that he had fallen and was not delivered by a complete death. They slandered the resurrection of the son of the widow of the only one, saying that he had fashioned death and was not overcome by the tyranny of death. They slandered the withered fig tree, saying it had been harvested and not withered by a masterly word. They slandered the changing of water into wine, saying that those at the supper were already intoxicated and did not know the mixture. They were not able to slander the resurrection of Lazarus alone.

They mourned for Lazarus; the man was prominent. They followed the lamentation, saw the tomb being sealed, and comforted according to custom, as if at a funeral feast of death, Martha and Mary, the sisters of Lazarus. They knew that he had been precisely four days in the tomb, having been laid there, and that a four-day corpse is everywhere decomposed, the flesh diminished, the bones exposed, the nerve-stability shattered, the entrails scattered, the stomach emptied. Realizing these things, when they saw the resurrection of Lazarus continuously whole, perfect as if from a potter, shining with re-living, they were disturbed.

They were quite despondent, not finding words of pretext, because this had prepared the reality of the Lord's resurrection to show how they would slander the resurrection of Lazarus. What is this, having prepared this for the reality of the Lord? Listen briefly. When Lazarus had naturally surrendered his present life, the Lord was not in Bethany present to the physical eyes.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
